text: dsh-tool-call-stats 是 DSH 插件，通过 tools/execute 和 tools/result 事件统计当前进程内各工具已提交调用的次数、错误数和平均调度耗时，并注册 tool_stats 工具以 JSON 数组及纯文本表格返回统计。适合查看本次运行中哪些工具使用较多、哪些调用报错或耗时较长；计数保存在进程内存中，不需要额外密钥或外部服务。

dsh-tool-call-stats counts committed tool calls, errors, and average dispatch duration per tool in the current DSH process. It listens to tools/execute and tools/result, then exposes tool_stats as JSON and a plain-text table. Counters stay in memory; no key or external service is required.
想查看当前 DSH 进程里每种工具调用了多少次、失败了几次。
帮我统计这次运行中各个工具平均花了多长时间。
Show me which tools were called, how often they errored, and their average duration in this run.
dsh-tool-call-stats 的功能「按工具汇总调用情况」：调用 tool_stats 后，返回每个工具已提交调用次数、错误次数及平均调度耗时，并按调用次数排序；结果同时可渲染为纯文本表格。

dsh-tool-call-stats README · dsh-tool-call-stats：[](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

A tiny community plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).

It records every committed **tool call** in the current harness process and exposes a `tool_stats` tool, so the model (or you) can ask at any point:

> Which tools were used, how often did they fail, and where did the time go?

dsh-tool-call-stats README · dsh-tool-call-stats：Not to be confused with the token/cost trackers in the ecosystem (`dsh-token-stats`, `dsh-usage-report`, ...) — this plugin counts **tool-call dispatches**, not tokens. Also unrelated to `dsh-tool-stat` (a descriptive-statistics math tool).

dsh-tool-call-stats README · dsh-tool-call-stats：> **Status**: built and verified end-to-end against the dsh v0.1 developer preview (headless profile, live DeepSeek session): both event listeners record real dispatches and `tool_stats` returns the table below. Upstream interfaces may still change during the preview.

Example output (from the verification run):

```
tool  calls  errors  avg_ms
----  -----  ------  ------
bash  1      0       23
read  1      0       8
dsh-tool-call-stats README · How it works：Everything in dsh is a plugin, and this one is deliberately minimal — three seams, ~100 lines, no build step:

dsh-tool-call-stats README · How it works：- `tools/execute` (waterfall): wraps each dispatch to record its start time, then delegates via `next()`.
- `tools/result` (observer): counts each committed result per tool name and accumulates duration; `result.isError` drives the error counter.
- `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`: exposes `tool_stats`, which returns a canonical JSON array (`output.schema`) and renders a plain-text table for the model.

dsh-tool-call-stats README · How it works：All state is in-memory and process-local. Nothing is persisted; restarting dsh resets the counters. When the plugin is unloaded, Cordis disposes both listeners and the tool automatically — no manual cleanup code.

dsh-tool-call-stats README · Into a profile (recommended)：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:disyli/dsh-tool-call-stats
```

pnpm ≥ 10 will ask you to allow the package before running install scripts (this package has none, but the prompt may still gate the git install). Follow the hint dsh prints, then re-run `add`.

Verify the layer and start:

```sh
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config   # shows a "# == dsh-tool-call-stats" layer
dsh --profile <name>
```

dsh-tool-call-stats README · As a local overlay (source checkout)：From a deepseek-harness checkout, point a patch at the local file:

```yaml

dsh-tool-call-stats README · stats.cordis.yml：- insert:
    - id: tool-stats
      name: '/absolute/path/to/dsh-tool-call-stats/index.js'
```

```sh
pnpm dsh web --patch ./stats.cordis.yml
```

dsh-tool-call-stats README · Use：Ask the agent things like:

- "Use tool_stats to show tool usage so far."
- "Which tool failed the most in this session?"

dsh-tool-call-stats README · Limitations：- Process-local only: counters reset on restart and are not shared across sessions.
- Calls aborted before the registry commits a result are not counted (their timing entries are garbage-collected after 10 s).
- Built against the dsh v0.1 developer preview; upstream interfaces may change ("THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES").
